subject: Close timeline: containment plan and procurement lag analysis
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finityhealth.com>
Cc: Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@finityhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Draft MAP & evaluation plan — target close Sept 30

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attaching an updated Mutual Action Plan and a suggested evaluation plan for the pilot. High level: we were targeting a Sept 30 close, with pilot completion by Sept 24 and production rollout in mid-Oct.

Outstanding procurement items I have on my side:
- Signed NDA (done)
- Security questionnaire (you noted engineering needs a final pass)
- PO or signed SOW to lock committed capacity

Can you confirm what your procurement timeline looks like — specifically the window for a PO issuance? If there is a procurement delay, we should proactively agree an alternative close plan so we don’t lose runway.

Next steps I propose:
1) You review MAP_v2.xlsx and comment on milestones you want moved.
2) We run a focused procurement call with your security lead this week to close the SOC/Q items.
3) If PO cannot arrive by 9/24, we propose a short rebaseline for the contract execution date and commit to reserved pilot capacity to protect performance pricing.

Files attached: MAP_v2.xlsx, pilot-schedule.ics

Best,
Neha

Thanks Neha — quick update from procurement and legal: they still need a scoped SOC2 excerpt and a short runbook for data residency. Our security team has a backlog and is estimating at least two weeks before they can sign off the questionnaire. PO issuance will likely be gated on that sign-off.

Proposition from our side: we can commit to finishing the pilot by Sept 24 internally, but we will not be able to generate a PO before ~Oct 8 unless security expedites.

If we push the contract signature beyond Sept 30 that’s fine as long as pricing and capacity are held steady and we have a written agreement on the evaluation acceptance criteria.

I attached the excerpt request (not an attachment here but noted). Happy to have a 30m call today with your security/ops lead.

—Priya
Director of Product | Finity Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Neha / Dylan — reading Priya’s note. Two thoughts for containment if procurement slips:

1) Two-track MAP: preserve the evaluation cadence (pilot completion 9/24) while decoupling contract execution date. We issue a formal rebaseline addendum that:
   - Keeps pricing and reserved pilot capacity for 30 days post original close date.
   - Defines acceptance criteria and sign-off owners for the pilot so there is no ambiguity.

2) Rapid evidence pack: I’ll pull SOC2 excerpt pages and a short data residency runbook (SOC2_excerpts.pdf) and a one-page procurement summary. We can send those to Priya’s security team by EOD tomorrow.

3) Commercial concession: as a show of good faith, we can offer a 30-day credit hold (applied if a PO isn’t in place by Oct 8) and a flexible invoice schedule. Need approval on whether this is within my delegated discount authority.

I created MAP_action_items.csv with owners and deadlines — attaching.

If we want to escalate, Neha should pull in VP Sales (Logan) to confirm concession authority and commit to supporting the procurement call.

Subject: Proposal: rebaseline contingency and pilot-first commitment (proposal attached)

Hi Priya / Ryan — thanks for the transparency. We want to keep momentum without forcing your security team into a rushed decision. Proposed binding steps:

1) Pilot-first commitment: Redwood will hold the reserved pilot capacity and pricing through Oct 28, 2026 if Finity signs the rebaseline addendum. Pilot acceptance criteria and milestones remain identical (pilot completion by Sept 24).

2) Rebaseline addendum: we will draft a one-page addendum that:
   - Moves contract signature to Oct 28, 2026 if PO issuance is delayed.
   - Confirms pricing, reserved capacity, and pilot acceptance criteria.
   - Includes a 30-day credit hold (applied if PO not in hand by Oct 8) to protect Finity from pricing movement.

3) Evidence pack: Marcus attached SOC2_excerpts.pdf and the MAP_action_items.csv; we will run a 30m security review tomorrow.

4) Exec alignment: if procurement indicates a hard block beyond Oct 8, Logan is prepared to join a procurement/finance call to remove bottlenecks on our side.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/FIN-2026-092 and I will send a DocuSign link for the rebaseline addendum for signature.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx, MAP_action_items.csv, SOC2_excerpts.pdf, pilot-schedule.ics

Please reply with acceptance of the rebaseline framework and preferred time for the security review.

Thanks,
Neha
